prompts_findings.prompt_lead: I want to author a test-strategy skill for this codebase. Ask me the questions y

risks_fired.evidence: In-fence structural enforcement, verbatim: 'Use the AskUserQuestion tool to interview me: one question per tool call, wait for my answer, then the next.' This is the catalog's strongest legal shape (a mechanical tool-call constraint), stronger than the body-callout carve-out in the template. Harm the rule guards against (Claude dumping all 7 topics as one form) is not present: the fence names the mechanism (tool, cadence) rather than just the outcome.
risks_fired.fix_hint: None needed; this is the reference-quality shape for the pattern.

risks_fired.evidence: In-fence 'Push back if my answer is generic' addresses Claude pushing on the STUDENT's answers. The body-callout mitigation for the complementary direction (Claude offering a weak default, student not pushing back) sits in the very next section: 'Push back when Claude offers a default you don't like. "No, we don't mock the database..." The push-back is where the skill gets its codebase truth.' Names the failure mode and the recovery move per the template's default-acceptance carve-out.
risks_fired.fix_hint: None needed; both directions of the pattern are named on the page (in-fence for student-answer generic-ness, in-body for Claude-offered defaults).

risks_fired.evidence: 'Show me before saving' gates a first-time write to `~/.claude/skills/test-strategy/SKILL.md`; nothing in this exercise or the module sequence establishes that file as pre-existing before this phase (the maintainer block's install-mechanic note treats the ship-destination bullet as the sole canonical statement of this path, and nowhere frames it as a re-run). Fresh-install-context carve-out logic applies by analogy even though this is authored-not-installed: no collision norm exists to imply.
risks_fired.fix_hint: None needed on the modal path; would only need a preserve-vs-replace clause if a future revision lets students re-run this exercise against an already-authored SKILL.md.

prompts_findings.prompt_lead: Invoke the `test-strategy` skill on this codebase and repository, on the code as

risks_fired.evidence: Evidence-backed Debrief carve-out applies: the fence asks Claude to grade a concrete artifact it just produced ("read the strategy you just produced") against four pointed diagnostic questions (generic-vs-specific, load-bearing tests named, integration boundary named, teammate-adequacy), and the body paragraph immediately after the fence names the bias mechanism by name ('same-window self-charity') and offers a concrete recovery move (the two-prompt fresh-read alternative, quoted verbatim in body). Harm the rule guards against (an unchallenged inflated self-grade) is closed by the named recovery move, not merely gestured at.
risks_fired.fix_hint: None needed; carve-out is fully satisfied — concrete artifact, pointed diagnostic questions, named bias, and a concrete alternative path.

risks_fired.evidence: Same body callout as self-report-inflation above satisfies this pattern's carve-out too: 'The grade is biased by design... same-window self-charity' names the charity mechanism directly, and the subsequent 'Sharpen the skill, not the output' + fresh-read alternative gives the student an actionable recovery.
risks_fired.fix_hint: None needed; same carve-out basis as self-report-inflation.

risks_fired.evidence: The self-grading questions in the fence are diagnostic/comparative rather than open praise-inviting ('does it read generic?', 'would a teammate... ask for more?'), which structurally discourages a softened answer. The adjacent body callout names the self-charity bias mechanism but does not use language like 'be blunt' or 'don't soften the answer' — it addresses the same-window bias, not tone specifically. Residual gap: a diplomatically-worded self-grade could still pass the stated questions without genuinely surfacing weakness.
risks_fired.fix_hint: Optional: one clause alongside the existing self-charity callout naming the softening/bluntness risk directly (e.g. 'be blunt about what's weak — a diplomatic answer defeats the exercise'). Not filed as blocking: the diagnostic question shape already resists praise-only answers, and Phase 2's body text goes on to ask the student to push on the skill's self-named weakest part, which is a second, independent check on the same failure.
